utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please stand up and make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just excuse me for one moment, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is your name Ivka Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you born on the 29th of September, 1944, in Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you a Bosnian Croat?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you still live in Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Have you lived there all of your life?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, occasionally I go to Zagreb for medical checkups and then I return, but I've been living in Uzdol since 1998 on a permanent basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. And the part of -- or the part of Uzdol in which you live, is it known as Kriz?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you have a son who was in the HVO in 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And is his name Janko? And he was born in --

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: He was born in November 1970, and was 22 in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In 1993, was the -- was the village area of Uzdol in HVO or Croatian control?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And was there a military campaign by the Bosnian army, the ABiH, against the HVO in that area?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were there front line positions around Uzdol occupied by the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How far were they from where you were living?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know much about such things. I'm not very educated. I'm just someone from a village, but it's about 200 metres as the crow flies. But when we went through that village by bus -- well, it's about a good 20 minutes, but there was a hill down below a little further away, and that is the hill that they were on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Right. I just want to show you several photographs and just get you to identify for the Trial Chamber some locations if you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown -- it's photo 0299-2311.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, while we're waiting for the photograph to appear, Mrs. Stojanovic, I'm just going to ask you to point out the locations in that particular photo. I'm going to ask you to point out Kriz, Uzdol, the church, the school, and Kovcalije.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 319.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Can you see that clearly?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's my house. And that's Kriz. That's Kovcalije.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The church is here. That's the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. We can't actually see what you're doing for a moment. I'd ask you to pause.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And make -- you can put some markings on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there are some markings there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's the church -- that's the school. This is the village of Kriz and this is my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can we just stop for one moment. Perhaps could that be erased. I want to put numbers on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could you erase that, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mrs. Stojanovic, I'm going to start again. I'm going to ask you to put numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, but just wait until we're ready to go. All right. Could you put a 1, a large 1, where the school is.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I think I made a mistake. Can I do it here?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Can you put a 2 where the church is, that's the Uzdol area.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, 3, the village or the hamlet of Kriz, just a 3 in the area where Kriz is.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Should I mark the house or something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, just the 3 -- we'll come to your house later. That's just to show where Kriz is. And also there's a place called Kovcalije.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Which number?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: 4, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And where you've put the 3, is that actually your house?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be received into evidence, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. There's no --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P320.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just wanted to show you another photo, just for an overview of that particular area, and that will be 0299-2307.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 321.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just have a look at that photograph on the screen, Mrs. Stojanovic. Can you see the village or the hamlet. Just look to your left. The usher will help you. Can you see in that photograph the village or hamlet area of Rajici and the village -- hamlet area of Kriz?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Rajici is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Can you please mark Rajici with a large 1.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And just so that we know exactly where we are, can you put a 2 over where Kriz is.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And without marking, can you also see your house in that particular photograph? I don't want you to mark on it, but can you see it there?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It's here, but you can't see it very well because the photograph was taken from a certain angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And can you see in that photograph where the ABiH front line positions were?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Bobari is here. They could have been up there, and they could have been up on Cer, but you can't see it very well. And this is where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You're indicating -- do you mean to the left of the edge of the photograph? That is where you think they were.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is Kriz. Our people were here and this is where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that also be received into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P322.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I've just been reminded. I forgot to ask for the originals to be admitted into evidence as well, Your Honour. Could they please be admitted into evidence separately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't think there's any problem, so it's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I've finished with the photographs for the moment, Mrs. Stojanovic. Where were you staying in July and August 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In July I was staying at my home until the 3rd of July. On the 3rd of July, Drago Ratkic was killed. An army arrived and said no one would stay there, no one should stay there, and that everyone had to find a way of leaving the village, only the troops were to remain there. So in the evening we went to Rama Rumboci. We were received there and we stayed there, but we nevertheless returned to our children to cook something for them and to do the washing. And that's how I was there on that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was your husband in July, August, and September 1993? Was he with you or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, at work. He was working.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he working in Bosnia or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He was working in Austria.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said "we stayed there." Are you referring to yourself and your children?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was there. I had a daughter married in the village. So I was taking care of her and my late mother since my brother died in 1992. His wife survived him and my mother and there was a handicapped daughter. And then I looked for a house I could stay in, and that's what happened. I went to the house to help my child to do the cleaning and then I returned. But that morning I didn't go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. I'm just trying to work out at the moment. You were staying in Rumboc. Are you saying that your son Janko was living in your house in Kriz?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, your mother, what was your mother's name?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Luca Zelenika.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What year was she born in?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Exhibit P298. It is a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was she living in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That would be in September. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's right. Up until she died, where was she living?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I took her to Rama on the 3rd of July. And she kept telling me that this was her third war and that she always provided the troops with food, with whatever she could provide them with. But she didn't pay any attention to that. She said, this was just an affair between neighbours. I wanted to go and see my daughter-in-law. As my son was on shift, he came to see me. He said, Mother, could you clean up for me a bit and we could pick some plums, but we could only go to that meadow in the evening because you could have thrown a stone from their lines to our lines --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mrs. Stojanovic --

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll come to that in a moment. Could I just go back for the moment to where your mother was living in September 1993.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I want to say that on that day I took her to see her daughter-in-law. That's what I want to say. My son came to see me. For that reason, I took her to see her daughter-in-law and to go to that house. It was a Sunday. I took her there, and she stayed there. Since I was closer to the line, I left her in Zelenike with her daughter-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: At which house did you leave her? Whose house was it?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Her house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is photograph -- is there a photograph on the screen to your left there in front of you?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You could see it before but you can't see it now. You could see Kovcalije before.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... right-hand corner --

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Wait a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We're going to enlarge a part of the photo for you.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. My sight isn't very good and I can't hear very well either. I'm a little deaf.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Does this enlargement help?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you see your mother's house there?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Is it one of those houses shown there above the church?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It's this little one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Right. Can you just put a circle around it and put a 1 underneath that.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You can't really see it. There's another house there. It should be there. I know these houses here. Just a minute. What should I put there?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Circle --

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Which number?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Circle the house and put a 1 underneath it.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you make it a little bit bigger, the 1?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, what about the Kazo Zelenika? Is he a relative of yours?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is he a cousin?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you see his house there?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's Kovcalije, that's Zelenike, this could be Kazo's house. What should I write down there?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just a 2.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. And is that area of those houses, is that the area known as Zelenike?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's all Zelenike. This entire area is called Zelenike.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be received into evidence, too?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. It's admitted into the evidence with the original.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The original is Prosecution Exhibit P298, which has been admitted already. And the one that is marked now is Prosecution Exhibit P323.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. I've finished with the photographs for the moment. Thank you. Now, you were telling the Trial Chamber a few moments ago that you took your mother to her house on the Sunday. What date was that?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It was the 12th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you yourself go to Uzdol on the 12th of September?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I went there to do the washing for my son, to make some bread. There was an orchard behind the house so I wanted to pick some plums. And the next Tuesday we wanted to take our mother back to Rumbok [as interpreted]. However, there was a bloodshed that morning and we were no longer able to.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said before that your son was staying in your house. Was anyone else staying in your house with him when you were in Rumboc, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't think there were any of my relatives in the house. Only some of them had returned from the front line and spent the night there. But other than that, there could not have been anyone to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why was your son staying in the house when you were staying elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Hold on. What exactly do you mean? Well, if my son is caught at the front line, he would probably have run away with the army, with the rest of his soldiers. Why should I have remained in the house all by myself? It wouldn't have been safe for me to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was your son an active member in the HVO in September 1993 when he was staying in the house and you were staying in Rumboc?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there any fighting in the area or did you notice anything that suggested there was fighting in the area when you were there on Sunday, the 12th of September?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: There was fighting then and earlier on. It was very often the case that we were in no position to spend the night there. We didn't dare. We would just take a short nap, but you always had to be alert, in a manner of speaking, because the fighting was so close.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What sort of fighting was there on the Sunday, the 12th of September? What did you see and hear?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It was like this: When I arrived on the 12th, my son came over to pick me up. I picked my mother up and left her there. If you show me that photograph again, I can show you the exact route I took. I was quite close to the front line, my own house, so I left her at my daughter-in-law's place. There was just a little random shooting on that day. On that evening, I couldn't bring myself to sleep. I saw lights flashing. And the next morning, the next Thursday morning, what happened was something that was beyond description.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What time did you wake the next morning? That's the morning of the -- the Monday?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, I hadn't even slept. And then I sort of woke up. I washed my son's bedlinen. I baked bread. He was at the front line, and once he returned in the evening I said, Shall we go and pick some plums? He said, Yeah, we might as well go and do that but we should be back home by 10.00, otherwise Dad will say that we didn't and we could have. The Monday evening I hadn't slept -- the night before I hadn't slept, so the Monday evening I fell asleep. I slept tight, as they say, and I was shaken awake by sounds of shooting, and that was Tuesday morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Tuesday, the 14th of September?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, 14th. It was a Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: At about what time was that?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When I opened the door across the way where my son was sleeping, I realised he was no longer there. He was at the doorstep holding a rifle shooting into the air. He said, Run, Mom, run, the whole village is on fire. It was half past 5.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it light or dark?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It was the month of September, so there was a little light. It was no longer that dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to say it here in the courtroom. I threw up. I realised the village was on fire and I got a change of clothes. That's the only thing I could think about at the moment: In case I die, at least I'll have fresh clothes on. He said, Mom, go to that orchard behind that abandoned house over there. I'll cover you and keep shooting into the air. Run and try to save your life. I ran there and a hand grenade exploded. It hadn't even occurred to us that there might be soldiers there. I just dashed out of the house. I took cover behind a neighbouring house. Just opposite me there was a huge man standing as tall as the sky it seemed. He said, Come over, Granny, we won't harm you. But no one every calls me granny. Everyone calls me my name, Zelenikusa. I took a look at him and realised that he was not one of ours. I took shelter -- I tried to take shelter behind the house, but I then I felt a burst of fire and I fell down and I lost consciousness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the -- this -- you just described a huge man standing -- standing nearby. What was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He was wearing a green uniform or at least that's what I thought. A green beret. He was very big, but it was all a flash. If I saw him now, I don't think I could possibly identify him. There was a lot of panic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did he appear to you to be a soldier?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I object to that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I object to that. It's a live issue in this case as to who were in the -- who were members of the forces that attacked these villages, so there should be no leading on that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the witness's previous answer I believe is quite clear: "He was wearing a green uniform or at least that's what I thought." So -- wait --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So I believe that this is the witness, herself's opinion. Whether he is a soldier or not is another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, frankly of course the witness can give her descriptions and I don't object to her doing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he armed?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was he armed with?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember the weapon at all, nor do I know anything about weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said earlier that you took a look at him and realised that he wasn't one -- "one of ours." What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When I looked at him, that was the impression I had. I was scared to death. I said he wasn't one of ours. If he had called me the way our people called me, I would have run straight to him and thrown myself into his arms, but I realised that he wasn't. I was thinking about running on, but I just fell down. And if you show me the photograph again, I can show you the exact house behind which I fell to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you felt a burst -- I withdraw that. I asked you earlier before whether you -- whether he appeared to you to be a soldier and you said yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think there was an objection to that question. My friend shouldn't be putting that to the witness. The objection was that the witness should be able to say what she said. Now I objected quite clearly to that question; now my friend has just repeated it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If I can be heard on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: If I could finish, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just in the middle of making an objection. Could I finish the objection and then my friend will have the full chance to respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honour. Your Honour, it's the issue of -- what was objected to at the time was the giving of an opinion as to whether the person was a soldier or some other class of armed person. And at the time the answer was not -- in my submission was not permitted. The question wasn't persisted with by my friend after I finished, and there was no answer to it, although the witness did of course attempt an answer in response. But now my friend is putting it as if it was a question and answer that was allowed on the record, and in my submission what I understood Your Honour to rule was different to that. Now, we better be clear. Perhaps we have misunderstood what Your Honour ruled about that. My objection was to the leading question concerning whether the person appeared to be a soldier. That was the objection at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Re, you may ask again a simple question, that is: What do you think that man was?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I certainly can. If there's a misunderstanding, I apologise. I didn't think Your Honour had ruled -- I thought Your Honour had ruled against Mr. Morrissey and the witness had actually answered the question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. But to have a clear record without any leading questions, you may ask the question in the way as I put it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mrs. Stojanovic, what did the man in the green uniform with the green beret appear to you to be?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It all happened in a flash. What do you expect me to say? It took no longer than a fraction of a second. There was a hill over there because there was another house built of concrete there. I saw that -- scared the living daylights out of me. I tried to take cover behind another house and then I fell down.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did the man who was armed, wearing a green uniform and a green beret, appear to you to be a civilian?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's a directly leading question in itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's capable of many answers: Yes, no, don't know. It doesn't suggest an --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think, you know, the witness did not answer your question directly. Maybe you could ask your question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We're after your opinion of what the man armed with the green uniform and the green beret appeared to you to be in that small time which you had to see him when he spoke to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Am I permitted to ask soldier or civilian? Okay, I won't ask that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Civilian, I don't think that would have been possible. I have never seen a civilian holding a gun in my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you heard the burst of fire, were there any other people in the area of where that man was armed?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How was I supposed to see that? I just dashed out and fell to the ground. It took no longer than a few seconds. I didn't have a chance to move about the village. I think you're asking the wrong question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know in which direction the burst of fire was fired?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. If you showed me the photograph, I'll show you exactly where I fell and where he called out to me from. And I'll show you the exact spot where I hit the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was the burst of fire directed in your direction or in another direction, if you can answer that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well -- no, Your Honours, I won't object to that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was fired in my direction and I was saved by the wall of that house. There was no way he could have gotten me because I fell down before he actually fired the shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What led you to conclude that it was fired in your direction?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, you said you fell to the ground. How long were you on the -- what happened? Tell the Trial Chamber what happened when you fell to the ground.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When I fell to the ground, I lost consciousness. I no longer knew what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you regain consciousness?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When I came to I wasn't able to breathe properly and I had a pain in my chest. My throat burned, so I couldn't swallow. I thought I was about to die and I thought that I had been wounded. At that moment, I heard a voice yelling, Omer, they have won. Then I thought either they'll take me away or they'll just kill me on the spot. I realised they had taken the village, and I fainted again.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you move from the spot where you originally went to the ground?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't even budge when he yelled, Omer, victory is ours. I didn't move at all, nor was I able to move for that matter. I just faked it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you heard one voice say, Omer, victory is ours. Were there any other voices?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No -- well, yes, perhaps. There was a clamour, but I failed to make anything out. When I woke up, I have no idea how long I had been lying there. And they said, This one is over and done with, and some other things that I decline to say before the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said there are other things you decline to say. Why would you decline to say what they said?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What exactly do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, you're in a court and it's okay to say what they said to you or said near you. We've probably heard -- heard these things before.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. All I'm saying is that when I came to I had heard earlier on that -- him saying, Come on, Omer, victory is ours. I thought they would slit my throat or take me away. What will become of me? And then I fainted. And later on I regained consciousness again, and they said, This one is dead. Fuck her mother. Get someone else instead. That's what they said.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And how were -- how were you lying? What was your position when they were saying this?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you want me to show it to you now?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, show it to us. That would be fine.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Right here?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The witness is, for the record, lying on the court floor on her stomach spreadeagled with her face pointing towards her left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you were lying there in the position you've just demonstrated, were you eyes open or closed?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you moving?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I wasn't able to. I tried to move, but I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And how many voices did you hear?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Later on --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: -- I no longer heard that many. I heard them saying that some livestock was on fire and that things were burning, that there was a stench in the air and I thought to myself, I'm done for. They have taken the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just go back to when you were lying there. You said you heard a voice saying, This one is dead. Fuck her mother. Get someone else instead. That's all they said. How many voices -- how many voices did you hear when that was said?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it a male voice or female voice?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Male, male.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you recognise the voice?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you able to see whether -- tell whether it was the same voice of the voice of the person who called out to you before and called you granny?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't recognise the voice. I was in a shock. I was really very scared.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And how long did you remain on -- in that spot, lying on your stomach with your eyes closed?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: There's no way I can know that. I had no watch on me. There was no -- no way I could have known.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Apart from the voices, what else could you hear when you were lying there?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. The smell of things burning, livestock, for as long as I was lying there. When I came to, I tried to move but I couldn't stand up, not right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You described hearing a burst of fire at the time when you went to the ground. Did you hear any shooting between then and when you were -- got up.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was shooting, and how. It went like that, tack, tack, tack, tack, tack. That's after I regained consciousness. I heard nothing while I was unconscious until I reached that bush.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you get to the bush?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say how much time had gone by, but I heard no more voices. I tried to crawl this way and that way. I hoped that I would be able to stand up. I thought that I'd go down as far as the church and maybe run into someone, one of our people, but I failed. I could only walk a couple of yards until I reached that bush.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was the shooting still going on at the time when you --

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But there was more shooting over near the school building. Our village had already burned down and they had already killed whoever they found. Anica's dead body was lying further down behind me, and there was Ante's dead body ahead of me, and there was not a living soul to be seen anywhere around.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll come back to that in a moment. I just want to go back to when you crawled towards the bush and there was shooting going on. How far away or how close did the shooting appear to be when you moved towards the bush?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if you are scared like I was, everything seems pretty close. When I reached the bush, I looked across the hill. There was a bit of woodland and a steep slope. I saw them coming down. I heard them singing and yelling where our soldiers had passed before.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who's "them"?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why do you think it was the Muslim army?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That was their line, their spot. It could not have been ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were they singing and yelling as they came past?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They were yelling and shouting saying all kinds of things. That's as much as I understood. But while I was in the bush, I heard them say things like, We'll chase the Ustasha as far down as Split.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you come to leave the bushes?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I thought to myself, God knows how many times, when I heard them singing, Why don't they just come back and kill me right here on the spot? I was afraid I would fall into their hands alive. My God, what should I do, I thought to myself? I looked over in the direction of my house to see if my son was still alive or dead. And I thought, Well, maybe it's just as well if he's dead; it's much better than they catching him alive. I looked at a nearby cowshed and there was a tree there. I thought to myself, You've nowhere left to run now. The shooting had stopped. There was some random shots being fired still, but not many. And then I heard someone closed to me saying, Look at this, look at this. And I thought to myself, my God, this is not possible. The Muslims are recording what they did. God, please send one of our soldiers so they may save me. And then I saw someone walk by carrying a camera on their left shoulder. And I thought to myself, oh my God, this may be one of ours. It was September and the leaves were dry, so the -- there was a rustling sound from the bushes where I was. One of them swung his rifle around, faced my way and said, Oh look, it's Ivka, she's still alive. That was the son of one of my cousins, Mato Ratkic. I burst into tears.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did they film you?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You mentioned a little earlier seeing some bodies in the village. I want you to tell the Trial Chamber where you were and where you went --

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- and whose bodies you saw, their family name and their given name.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When I stood up to see whether I should be in my way [as interpreted] I turned around to see if there was any soldiers behind me. I saw Anica's body behind me and ahead of me Ante's dead body. That's where I was. But further down behind me there was more bodies which I only saw later.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What is Anica's family name?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Anica Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the Ante?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Ante Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you see any other bodies?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't on that occasion, not then. But when they found me then I saw Kata Ratkic, Martin Ratkic, but I didn't see Franjo Stojanovic and Serafina Stojanovic who were prostrated or behind Anica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the Rajic family?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When they found me and I started crying and they said that I would go with them. We went down to the church. I saw the Rajics there, four of them, and I saw the other two in the house while I was passing by.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What are the names of the four people you saw of the Rajic family?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sima Rajic, Mara Rajic, Stanko Rajic, and Lucija Rajic, Mijo Rajic, and Ivka Rajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you with the people doing the videoing when you saw those bodies?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said your mother died on that day. Where was she killed?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In her house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you see -- did you go to her house that day?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you see --

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They wouldn't let me. They wouldn't let me go there since when they took me to the school I was in a state of shock. I couldn't even have gone. They said, Don't go anywhere. You won't be going anywhere. And they took me away somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you see your mother's body?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't, not then.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did she have a funeral?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They were killed on the 14th. They were in Split for ten days where an autopsy was performed. I can't remember the dates, but I think that they were buried around the 20th but not in our cemetery. That was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: This question may sound a little strange, but was your mother born in 1906, did she have a weapon or was she to your knowledge taking part in any hostilities in war?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. And there's something else I'll tell you. She said, What are you afraid of? This is my third war. I've always provided the troops with food and made them see to their own business. Take me to my house so that I can see my daughter-in-law. And then what happened to her happened to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just want to go back to your seeing the bodies of the Rajic -- members of the Rajic family. You said you saw Ivka Rajic and Mijo Rajic's bodies.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you see Mijo's body?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We saw Mijo's body in his house, on the threshold. And the late Ivka, she had suffered from a stroke and she was killed in her bed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was she someone who was able to leave her bed?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And very briefly, where did you go after seeing these bodies and when the filming was going on?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Having seen the bodies, we entered the church because they had shot at the images, and that's what they filmed. We then went to the school, but shooting broke out. Later we approached the school, and then they told a driver to drive more quickly, that assistance had to be provided. And I was taken to Rama.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown photograph -- Exhibit P306.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What should I point to here?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, I want you to show the Trial Chamber places you went when you left your house and there was the shooting on the morning of the 14th of September. Firstly, I want you to just mark your own house again. Put a 1 where your own house is.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to draw an arrow in the direction of where you walked. If you do a --

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the house?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No. What I want you to do is to sketch little lines, like dot, dot, dot, dot, dot, with an arrow, showing the route you took.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Once I had left the house, you want me to show the route I took?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please. With a broken line and an arrow so we know which direction you went.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Here. I'll do it like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you put an arrow at the end of it so we know which direction.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mrs. Stojanovic, look this way --

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You see I'm holding up an arrow.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. My hand is shaking. I can't really do it properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You're doing fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If the record could reflect that the line goes from the house marked 1, around the back of another house, into some bushes sort of to the upper right, and that's the direction in which she indicated she was travelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Stojanovic, where were you when you saw the large man wearing the green uniform with the green beret? Where were you and where was he? You've just put a circle. What I want you to do is put a --

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's where he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you mark -- maybe make that into a 2?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where he was. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, please, a 2.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Right. And where were you? Please -- please draw yourself in with a circle and a number 3 -- a dot meaning where you were, a circle where you were, a small one --

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Number 3, where I was?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That -- that appears to be just in front of the white house, which is the second house directly above your own. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And where did you fall to the ground? Can you show us where you fell to the ground?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I can. I can. What should I put down there at the spot where I fell to the ground?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you make that a little bit larger? We have to look at this afterwards when you're not here anymore.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I think so. Now, you said -- you said a burst of fire -- sorry, a burst -- there was a burst of fire when you fell to the ground.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In which direction was the shot fired, if you can tell us.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When I was there when this person called out to me, I fell there immediately. I only heard a burst of fire that had been opened in my direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And on the -- you've drawn that line which goes into the bushes. Is that where you crawled to?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just put a --

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I crawled. There was here where I fell before this -- in front of this white house. And then I reached the stables and that's where I took shelter. That's where they found me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Right. Can you just put a 5 where that was.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean at the spot in the bushes where I was?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You described earlier hearing a voice saying -- the only words unfortunately that are sticking in my mind at the moment are: Fuck your mother, and something like, This one's dead. It will take me a moment to find the exact portion of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just can't remember exactly what she said. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which spot -- is that spot marked on the photograph where you were when you heard that being said?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where I was lying?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that the spot marked 4?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I think so. The white house is number 4. Can I mark the white house itself? It will be clearer for you then.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What do you want to do on the white house? Do you want to make the 4 clearer?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mark it with number 4 so that you can know that that is where I was lying.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yeah, if you could make it clearer, the exact spot where you were lying, it would help.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's fine. The question is: When you heard the voices saying those things -- or the voice saying those things, was that where you were or was it in another spot?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's where I heard that -- that's where I was lying when they cursed my mother. And I lost consciousness there on a couple of occasions. That's when I heard all of that. But when I was in the bushes, marked number 5, then I heard them singing, crying out, and saying, Run, Ustasha, all this territory is ours as far as Split.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be received into evidence, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. So it's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P324.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I wish to show the witness a portion of video P312, which was admitted into evidence yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mrs. Stojanovic, you gave evidence earlier about the death of your mother and marked on a photograph where she lived. I'm going to show you a portion of the video and ask you if you can recognise something.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We started at timer 24.58.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I -- could I just ask what part of the transcript that is?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's a transcript of this -- this interview -- of this video, and I just want to know what part of the transcript this passage appears in.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The -- we've synchronised the transcript with the video overnight, so it will appear underneath, if that assists, on screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It assists. I just want to know which part is going to be played so I can follow. Which part -- if I can just ask which page that part of the transcript is going to be, I can follow, both on the screen and on my marked copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I think it's page 11 and 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, thanks. I'm grateful for that indication. I think this is a part where the witness doesn't actually appear herself in the video, but if it's a question of getting her to identify a particular house, I don't object to it being shown, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll see.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, it most certainly is, yes. Can the video please be shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just stop it there. We've stopped at 25.05.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you recognise that house, Mrs. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Whose house is that?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's my mother's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Stop there. Stop at -- we've stopped at 25.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right, Mrs. Stojanovic, there's a body in that photograph -- in that video. Do you recognise whose body that is?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It's my mother's body.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How do you recognise it to be your mother's body?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I can recognise the house and also recognise the item of clothing I made for her. She was also wearing a sort of national costume. Her head has been disfigured, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that an appropriate time for a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you finish showing the video?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's two more short clips I want to show.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's continue to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I will do so. Could we please show -- before we go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know Ivan Zelenika, Jadranka Zelenika, and Ruza Zelenika?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Can I just intervene here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this witness, as I understand it, was not shown those people in the state they were in. Now, if I'm wrong about that, if the witness did see them in the state they were in at that time, I've got no objection. But frankly, to show it to this witness when she didn't see it before, those photographs are very distressing ones, and I fail to see any use in showing it to this witness. I have no difficulty to it being shown to the Tribunal generally. I'm just not sure what this witness can be add in the least to it. And frankly I object to her -- to this witness being shown those terrible photographs, if it is those photographs showing Jadranka and the others because it just serves no purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. What is the purpose of showing those pictures to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The objection I don't understand. The fact that the photographs might be distressing is not a valid objection in my respectful opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, I'm asking you what is the purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The purpose is identification of the people in the video. Yesterday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Only for the identification?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please, you may show it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We're starting at P312 at 34.40.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: 34.44. Just stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There is the body of a man. Do you recognise that person?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's Ivan Zelenika.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We stopped at 35.25.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Jadranka.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Jadranka Zelenika. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Jadranka Zelenika.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Stop there. That's 36.25.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Riza Zelenika -- Ruza Zelenika.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Stop there. Thank you. There is another portion I wish to show her of which she is in. That will take about five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take a break and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We will continue to show this last portion of the video, which is Exhibit P312.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A little earlier, Mrs. Stojanovic, you told the Trial Chamber that you were filmed coming out of the bushes. I wish to show you that portion of the video now starting at 43.06.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just pausing there for one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That is you coming out of the bushes, isn't it, running out of the bushes?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That portion of the video we just saw to 46.17, was that the -- that was you coming out of the bushes and explaining what had happened to Mato.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you also mentioned some bodies -- I'll just play a little bit more of that video. Were you present when these bodies were filmed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This, this is Anica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's Anica Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Stop there. 48.20 we've stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who's house is that one? In which part of Uzdol is that?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: These are the Rajics -- or rather, this is the hamlet of Rajici. The house belongs to Pero Prskalo. There was a concrete area outside the house. Here you can see Sima Rajic; her daughter, Mara Rajic; Stanko Rajic; and his life Lucija Rajic. Jela Dzalto was burned alive in that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Those three bodies that were shown a moment ago as 48.39, were those the three bodies you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll just go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Stop there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Four bodies. The daughter and the mother and the wife. And Jela was burned alive in that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's at 48.39.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's a body shown at time of 49.04. Do you recognise that person?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This could be Lucija, but it's a dead body, difficult to recognise. If the image was a bit clearer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Stanko's wife, yes, Lucija.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Lucija Rajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Lucija Rajic. Is her last name or family name, Rajic?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the man lying on the ground next to her at 49.30.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Stanko Rajic, Lucija's husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: 49.50, who is that?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is Sima Rajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: At 50.17, do you recognise that person?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This one?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mara Rajic, Sima's daughter.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The four bodies you've just seen, Lucija Rajic, Stanko Rajic, Sima Rajic, and Mara Rajic, were those people -- were those people civilians or were they military?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were civilians, but I'm not sure about Mara Rajic. She worked as a cook there. I'm not sure about her. The rest of them were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We'll continue with the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: At 51.08, do you recognise the body of that person?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mijo Rajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he a civilian or military to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Civilian. He had a wife who had suffered a stroke nine years previously. She had no one else but him, so he had to take care of her.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Stopping at 51.36.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's a body inside a house. Whose body is that?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is Mijo's wife. She had been sick for nine years. She had suffered a stroke.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was her name?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Ivka Rajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And finally, there's a house at 51.50. Whose house is that?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I really can't remember right now. If I can have a minute to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did that help?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you don't know, no matter. We'll worry about that.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've also identified -- or sorry, described seeing the bodies of Anica and Ante Stojanovic. Were they civilians or military?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And just for the completeness, the video we've just shown you from P312, were you with the people when they were videoing it and seeing the -- finding those bodies?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Anica and Ante and the one near the school, the one named Rajic, I was with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And just for completeness of this, was it at that point in the video which is on the screen at about 51.50 that the video camera went one way and you went the other way? That is, they went off to continue videoing and you went elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's the evidence in-chief, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any cross-examination, Mr. Morrissey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much, Mrs. Stojanovic. My name is Peter Morrissey. I am counsel looking after Mr. Halilovic in this case. I just want to ask you a question about that videotape before I come to my normal questions and that is: Were you present when they were video recording anything at the church?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was in the church with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And when did that take place? Was it after the scenes that have just been shown to you by the Prosecutor or before that time?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When they took me from the village once they had found me we were off to the church which is near Rajici. We entered the church so they could film the damage inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you see any more dead bodies after that time while you were with the camera?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, not after. They didn't let me continue with them. They realised the state I was in, that I was losing it. We went as far as the school. We waited a while because there was still some shooting. That was how far we got, and they said, You should go back and rest and get some help. So at that point they took me back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When you say they took you back, you mean they took you back to Prozor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, I have to ask you some -- I have to ask you some questions about the hamlet of Kriz during the time of the war. First of all, was there a front line between the HVO and the Bosnian army along a hill named Borak at that time?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You're asking me about whether there was any fighting going on?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No. I'm asking you about the position of the front line at the time when you made the visit.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean before when I was there or later? Which is it you want me to talk about?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: During your visit when you came on the 12th of September and in the couple of days before the killings took place, was there a front line, a war zone effectively --

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And was that position a hill --

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, war zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And was there a line --

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Our people were at Borak and their people were at Krstiste which is a hill next to Borak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And the young men -- well, I'll come to the young men in the village in just a minute. But how far from your house was the front line held by the HVO at Borak? Was it about 200 metres away?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It was close to the village itself. How far were they? All I can tell you is that I was outside my house, a shell came from over there, and it hit a lamp in my house but not me. So that's how far they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, I would like the witness to be shown a photograph, MFI 319. It might be tendered already as P319.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You're going to be shown a photograph that you've already looked at and I'm going to ask you for some comments about that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, we may have wrongly noted the exhibit number here, but the photo on the screen is not the one we want. Could I just provide the photograph number and that might assist you if we're got our numberings wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mrs. Stojanovic, would you forgive me for a moment, we have a technical issue to resolve.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, the one I have a numbered in the top right-hand corner 0402-0932. I have it labelled as MFI 319 but that must be wrong.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Prosecution Exhibit P306.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm grateful for the assistance of the court staff. And could I have Prosecution Exhibit P306 shown to the witness, Mrs. Stojanovic. Thank you. We have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Mrs. Stojanovic, looking at that picture, as you do now, is the area called Borak visible?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, not in this one; it's further off. This is the village and this is my orchard where the plum trees. And it's outside this image.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. What I would like you to do is to draw an arrow on the edge of that photograph pointing to where Borak is located.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You can't see it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand that. It would just help us, though, if you pointed -- if you showed the direction by drawing an arrow where it is.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But there was a shot that I looked at where one could actually see Borak, but it wasn't this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, that's okay. I may ask you to look at that photograph soon. On this picture, though, would you just please draw an arrow pointing in the direction where Borak is located.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I drew a circle right there, so it's in that direction. It's in the direction of the small circle that I drew and then further off.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you for doing that. Next of all, would you please mark with the number 1 your house, as you did earlier.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You want me to draw a line or how should I mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just write the numeral 1 on your house, please.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. That's exactly what I wanted. Would you please now mark with a numeral 2 - just wait for a moment -- well, before I ask you to mark it. Did your son, Janko, have a friend named Mato who was living in a house nearby?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would you please mark --

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They were born the same year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Would you please mark that house with the number 2.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where Mato was you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Very well. Now, would you please mark with the number 3 where it was that you last saw your son, Janko, when you ran away? Where was he when you last saw him?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I saw Janko outside my house, at this corner. And this is an abandoned house, the one I'm pointing at now. There was a flower bed there. He jumped straight behind the flower bed and said, Mother, I'll start firing into the air and you just run. This is the house. Should I put a number there?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would you please put a dot where you last saw him, just a point where you last saw him.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And just write a number 3 next to that point and then I've finished with the markings on this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could I perhaps suggest that be given a 3. It may become a little bit unclear, the dot -- the dot on the house next to the 2 when these are printed out later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I thought that was what I just asked to happen, but perhaps I'm wrong. But in any event, my learned friend and I are on completely the same path here, so that's what I was hoping I had asked. Anyway, perhaps I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would you mind just putting the numeral 3 next to that dot to help us to remember later.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you rub this out. This is the house. Number 3, is that right? Which number should I mark that with?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, it's just that you put a dot where your son --

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. You can rub that out, if the machine will let you do that. Yes, please do. Rub it out and put where you -- put where he really was. With a dot.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The dot marks the place where he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And would you just put a number 3 right next to that dot.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thanks. And actually -- sorry, there is just one other thing. Could you just put with another dot where the man with the green beret was.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And could you mark that with a little number 4.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I offer that document for tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So it's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you for your help in that regard, Mrs. Stojanovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the Court Deputy will tell us the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D235.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, I just have some questions first of all about the people living in Kriz at the time when this tragedy happened. Were there any of -- any young men of military age living in Kriz at that time who were not members of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could I -- I'm reluctant to interpose here, but my learned friend has asked the witness a question which is really one of -- has a legal characterisation, that is, of military age. If the witness is capable of answering it, she must first -- establish that she knows what military age is or I wonder if my learned friend could put a range of ages to her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour, I'll clean it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Were there any male people in that village between the age of 16 and 50 that were not in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In that village you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In Kriz.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes -- well, there was Zoran Stojanovic. He was under age. There was Ivan Stojanovic; he was also under age. They were all the sons of the late Anica, who had been killed. But I don't know whether there were any other young men. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And of those two individuals -- the two individuals, the young boys that you mentioned there, do you ever recall seeing those boys with a weapon in their hand?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did either of them know how to fire a weapon to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was your son living in that village at that time?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Janko.

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes -- well, yes, he was a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And when he was off duty, did he -- was it his practice to sleep in your home there?

utterances.speaker: IVKA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Up until 1993, up until the 14th, that's when he was wounded and then he spent time in hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And was it your practice to visit him from time to time there at his request to help him by cleaning and cooking?
